newsitem.title: POLAND: ESPEBEPE PLUNGES BEFORE CREDITORS MEET.
newsitem.headline: ESPEBEPE PLUNGES BEFORE CREDITORS MEET.

text.p: Polish construction firm Espebepe fell the daily maximum 10 percent to 7.65 zlotys after a newspaper article on Wednesday said one of the firm's creditors would seek the firm's bankruptcy in court.
Espebepe has 75 million zlotys in debt divided among 564 creditors, who meet on Friday to discuss a possible debt write-off deal.
"I don't think it's such a big deal that one small creditor applied to the court but it probably had an effect on the stock's price today," Ryszard Wojnowski, analyst at PBI bank brokerage, said.
No Espebepe official was immediately available for comment.
The bourse said after the market's close that it would not trade in Espebepe on Friday because of the creditors' meeting.
Traders said the strong selling after price fixing, in which investors had their bids reduced, suggested the stock would fall again on Thursday.
